chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raising it, said,
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The reproach demolishes the favour'.

key_terms.الْمَنُّ: Reproach or embarrassing the recipient of a favour

ai.seo_question: What does 'Al-Man' mean in Islamic ethics and how does it affect charity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *al-man* (reminding of a favor), explaining that it nullifies the spiritual reward of the good deed (*al-sani'ah*). This teaching is deeply rooted in the Shia tradition of *adab al-sadaqah* (etiquette of charity), where the internal intention and external demeanor must both preserve the dignity of the recipient to ensure the act is accepted by Allah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The reproach (embarrassing the recipient) demolishes the favour’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah in a marfu‘ manner the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Embarrassing a recipient, after giving charity destroys the virtue of this benevolent deed.’”
